book_name: 新标准大学英语综合教程3

words.ex: His acceptance of the offer made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了这份提议，让大家都很高兴。
words.en: The act of agreeing to receive or undertake something offered.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.tr: adj. 开始发育（发展）的；初露头角的； v. “bud”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is a budding artist who loves to paint.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位刚开始发展艺术才能的画家。
words.en: A budding artist, writer, etc. is someone who is starting to show skill or talent in that area.

words.ex: The old cemetery is near the church.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地在教堂附近。
words.en: A cemetery is a place where dead people are buried.

words.ex: The coastal village has beautiful beaches.
words.ex_cn: 这个沿海村庄有美丽的海滩。
words.en: relating to the coast, the area where the land meets the sea

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.ex: The children played on the deck of the ship.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在船的甲板上玩耍。
words.en: A deck is a floor-like surface on a ship, or a set of cards used in games. It can also mean to decorate or adorn something.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: His speech was very impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲非常令人印象深刻。
words.en: Something that is impressive makes you admire it because it is very good, large, important, etc.

words.tr: adj. 很长的；漫长的；冗长的；
words.ex: The meeting was lengthy and tiring.
words.ex_cn: 会议很长，很累人。
words.en: Something that is lengthy lasts for a long time, often longer than you want or expect.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.tr: adj. 富有成效的；多产的；生产的；
words.ex: He had a productive day and finished all his work.
words.ex_cn: 他度过了富有成效的一天，完成了所有工作。
words.en: Producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.

words.tr:
n. 后部；
v. 饲养；抚养；
adj. 后面的；
words.ex: The rear of the car was damaged in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的后部在事故中受损了。
words.en: The back part of something, especially a building or vehicle; to bring up and care for a child until they are fully grown.

words.ex: The people showed resistance against the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 人们对这项不公平的法律表示抵抗。
words.en: Resistance is the refusal to accept or comply with something; the attempt to prevent something by action or argument.

words.ex: He wrote a script for a short movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部短片写了剧本。
words.en: A script is the written form of a play, film, or broadcast. It includes the dialogue and stage directions.

words.tr:
n. 激浪；拍岸浪花；
v. 冲浪；（互联网上）冲浪；
words.ex: He bought a new surf for the beach trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为海滩之旅买了一块新的激浪。
words.en: To surf means to ride on the crest of a wave towards the shore, typically on a surfboard. It can also mean to browse the internet.

words.tr:
v. 成为三倍；使增至三倍；
n. 三倍的数；三个一组；
adj. 三部分的；
words.ex: The company's profits tripled last year.
words.ex_cn: 该公司去年的利润增长了三倍。
words.en: To triple something means to make it three times as much in size or number.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.tr:
n. 烈火；火焰；闪耀
v. 闪耀；熊熊燃烧；发亮光
words.ex: The fire began to blaze in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 火在森林里开始猛烈燃烧。
words.en: A blaze is a very large or fiercely burning fire that is difficult to control.

words.ex: He nodded in a blink.
words.ex_cn: 他一眨眼就点了点头。
words.en: To shut and open the eyes quickly, typically involuntarily.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.ex: The consumption of water has increased this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年水的消耗量增加了。
words.en: Consumption is the act of buying and using products.

words.tr:
n. 接触；联系；
v. 接触；联系；
words.ex: The two balls made contact when they collided.
words.ex_cn: 两个球在碰撞时发生了接触。
words.en: Contact refers to the act of communicating with someone, especially regularly, or the state of touching something.

words.ex: The continual rain made the road very muddy.
words.ex_cn: 不停的雨让道路变得非常泥泞。
words.en: Something that is continual happens repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: He gave a definite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了肯定的答案。
words.en: If something is definite, it is firm and clear, and unlikely to be changed.

words.tr: phrase. 依赖于……的；取决于……的
words.ex: The plant is dependent on sunlight to grow.
words.ex_cn: 这种植物依赖阳光生长。
words.en: If one thing is dependent on another, the first thing will be affected or determined by the second.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.tr:
v. 咯咯地笑
n. 咯咯笑；趣事
words.ex: The children giggle when they see the clown.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们看到小丑时咯咯笑。
words.en: To laugh in a silly, often high-pitched way, especially in a nervous or embarrassed manner.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.ex: He is largely responsible for the project's success.
words.ex_cn: 他主要对这个项目的成功负责。
words.en: To a great extent; mostly.

words.ex: He wiped his mouth with a napkin.
words.ex_cn: 他用纸巾擦了擦嘴。
words.en: A napkin is a piece of cloth or paper used at meals to protect your clothes and to wipe your mouth and fingers.

words.ex: He has a clear notion of right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他对对错有清晰的概念。
words.en: A notion is an idea or belief about something.

words.tr: n. 局外人；无取胜希望者；
words.ex: He felt like an outsider at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上感觉像个局外人。
words.en: An outsider is someone who does not belong to a particular group or organization.

words.ex: The machine makes a perpetual noise.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发出持续的噪音。
words.en: Something that is perpetual continues indefinitely or for a very long time without interruption.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

words.tr:
n. 提示；
v. 促使；
adj. 迅速的；准时的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a prompt to help students start writing.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了一个提示，帮助学生开始写作。
words.en: If you prompt someone when they stop speaking, you encourage or help them to continue. If you are prompt to do something, you do it without delay or you are not late.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: There is a resemblance between the two brothers.
words.ex_cn: 这两兄弟之间有相似之处。
words.en: If there is a resemblance between two people or things, they are similar to each other.

words.tr:
n. 标签；标记；
v. 加标签于；
words.ex: The tag on the shirt says 'wash cold'.
words.ex_cn: 衬衫上的标签写着‘冷水洗涤’。
words.en: A tag is a small piece of card, cloth, or plastic which is attached to an object or person and has information about that object or person on it. A tag can also be a word or phrase that is used to describe or identify something, especially in a computer file or on a website.

words.tr: v. 诱惑；引诱；怂恿；劝诱；
words.ex: The smell of cookies tempted him to eat one.
words.ex_cn: 饼干的香味诱惑他吃了一块。
words.en: If something tempts you, it makes you want to have it or do it, even though you know you should not.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

words.tr:
v. 跌倒；摔倒；暴跌
n. 摔倒；混乱；暴跌
words.ex: The child tumble down the stairs.
words.ex_cn: 孩子从楼梯上跌倒了。
words.en: If someone or something tumbles, they fall quickly and suddenly, often turning over or spinning as they fall.

words.tr:
v. （使）回旋；（使）旋转
n. 一连串的事；混乱；尝试
words.ex: The wind makes the leaves whirl around.
words.ex_cn: 风让树叶旋转飞舞。
words.en: To move or cause to move rapidly around and around.

chapters.name: Unit 3 - Art for art's sake - Vocabulary

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.tr:
n. 委员会；佣金；
v. 委托；
words.ex: The commission met to discuss the new law.
words.ex_cn: 委员会开会讨论新法律。
words.en: A commission is a group of people who have been appointed to find out about something or to control something, or the act of doing this. It can also refer to a sum of money that is paid to someone for selling something, which is usually a percentage of the value of the goods sold.

words.ex: He is a composer who writes music for movies.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位为电影作曲的作曲家。
words.en: A composer is a person who writes music, especially classical music.

words.ex: He didn't study, consequently he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他没有学习，因此考试不及格。
words.en: As a result; therefore.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: v. 参与；从事；吸引；与…建立密切关系；
words.ex: He engages in community volunteer work.
words.ex_cn: 他参与社区志愿工作。
words.en: To engage means to occupy, attract, or involve someone or oneself in a particular activity or situation.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.ex: He studied hard for the sake of his family.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习是为了家人。
words.en: If you do something for the sake of something, you do it for that purpose or in order to achieve that result.

words.ex: He grinds the coffee beans into powder.
words.ex_cn: 他把咖啡豆碾成粉末。
words.en: To reduce something to small particles or powder by crushing it.

words.ex: He cooked dinner; meantime, the kids did their homework.
words.ex_cn: 他做晚饭；与此同时，孩子们在做作业。
words.en: The time between one event and another; meanwhile.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.ex: The needle will pierce the skin.
words.ex_cn: 针会刺穿皮肤。
words.en: If a sharp object pierces something, or if you pierce something with a sharp object, the object goes into it and makes a hole in it.

words.ex: He painted a portrait of his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他画了一幅他母亲的肖像。
words.en: A portrait is a painting, drawing, or photograph of a particular person.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的； v. 取得资格；“qualify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a qualified teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有资格的老师。
words.en: Having the necessary qualifications for a particular job or task.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.ex: The scandal made the news last week.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻上周上了新闻。
words.en: A scandal is a situation or event that is thought to be shocking and immoral and that everyone knows about.

words.ex: He sings and plays guitar simultaneously.
words.ex_cn: 他一边唱歌一边弹吉他。
words.en: If two or more things happen simultaneously, they happen at exactly the same time.

words.ex: The water is sufficiently warm to swim.
words.ex_cn: 水温足够暖和，可以游泳。
words.en: To an adequate degree; enough.

words.ex: The viewer watched the movie on TV.
words.ex_cn: 观看者在电视上看了这部电影。
words.en: A viewer is someone who watches something, especially television.

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.ex: He drives an automobile to work every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天开车去上班。
words.en: A vehicle that is powered by an engine and is used for carrying passengers on roads.

words.tr:
v. 敢说；
n. 打赌；赌注；
words.ex: I bet you didn't know that.
words.ex_cn: 我敢说你不知道那件事。
words.en: If you bet on the result of a horse race, football game, or other event, you give someone a sum of money which they give you back with extra money if the result is what you predicted, or which they keep if it is not.

words.tr: v. 自夸；夸耀；自豪地拥有
words.ex: He boasts about his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他夸耀自己的新车。
words.en: If someone boasts about something that they have done or that they own, they talk about it very proudly, in a way that other people may find irritating or offensive.

words.ex: The university conferred an honorary degree on him.
words.ex_cn: 大学授予他一个荣誉学位。
words.en: To confer something such as a degree or an honor on someone means to give it to them in a formal way. To confer with someone means to discuss something with them in order to make a decision.

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.ex: The old man muttered a curse under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 老人低声嘟囔了一句诅咒。
words.en: A curse is a word or sentence that is used to wish evil or harm on someone or something.

words.tr: v. 不赞成；反对；不同意
words.ex: My parents disapprove of my choice.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母不赞成我的选择。
words.en: If you disapprove of something, you have a negative opinion of it, often because you think it is wrong or not suitable.

words.ex: He majors in economics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修经济学。
words.en: Economics is the study of the way in which money, industry, and trade are organized in a society.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: n. 眼界; 范围; 地平线( horizon的名词复数 ); 界限
words.ex: Travel broadens our horizons.
words.ex_cn: 旅行开阔了我们的眼界。
words.en: The line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet; the limit of a person's mental perception, experience, or interest.

words.ex: His ignorance of the rules caused the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的无知导致了这个错误。
words.en: Lack of knowledge or information.

words.tr: n. 含意；可能的影响（或后果）；暗示；
words.ex: The implication of his words was that he was sorry.
words.ex_cn: 他话中的含意是他很抱歉。
words.en: An implication is a possible future effect or result of an action or decision, often one that is not immediately obvious.

words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr: n. 废旧杂物；无价值的东西；
words.ex: He cleaned up the junk in his garage.
words.ex_cn: 他清理了车库里那些废旧杂物。
words.en: Old or discarded articles that are considered useless or of little value.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.tr: n. 痴迷；困扰；着魔；强迫观念；
words.ex: His obsession with video games made him ignore his studies.
words.ex_cn: 他对电子游戏的痴迷让他忽略了学业。
words.en: An obsession is an idea or thought that continually preoccupies or intrudes on a person's mind.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.ex: He gave her a scowl when she was late.
words.ex_cn: 她迟到时，他皱了皱眉。
words.en: When someone scowls, they look at someone or something with an angry or irritated expression.

words.ex: The stability of the table prevents it from wobbling.
words.ex_cn: 桌子的固定防止它摇晃。
words.en: The state of being stable; the quality of being unchanging.

words.tr: adj. 令人惊愕的； v. “stagger”的现在分词；
words.ex: The staggering cost of the project surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目令人惊愕的费用让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: Something that is staggering is very surprising and shocking.

words.ex: They live in a quiet suburb outside the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市外一个安静的市郊。
words.en: A suburb is a residential district located on the outskirts of a city.

words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr: v. 使可见；使形象化；设想；
words.ex: He uses maps to visualize the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用地图来使数据可见。
words.en: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

chapters.name: Unit 5 - A place in society - Vocabulary

words.ex: The weather was agreeable for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气令人愉悦，适合散步。
words.en: Pleasant and easy to like; willing to agree to something

words.ex: The audience gave applause after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: Applause is the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands to show approval or enjoyment.

words.ex: He is a competent teacher who helps students easily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有能力的老师，能轻松帮助学生。
words.en: If you are competent to do something, you have the skills, abilities, or experience necessary to do it well.

words.ex: He beat his competitor in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: A competitor is a person, team, or company that is competing against others, especially in business or sports.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.tr:
n. 核；核心；重点；
adj. 核心的；
words.ex: The core of the apple is not edible.
words.ex_cn: 苹果的核心不能吃。
words.en: The central or most important part of something.

words.ex: The government punished the official for corruption.
words.ex_cn: 政府因贪污惩罚了那名官员。
words.en: Corruption is dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in positions of power.

words.ex: The delivery of the package took three days.
words.ex_cn: 这个包裹的交付花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of delivering letters, parcels, or goods.

words.ex: The hospital received a donation of books.
words.ex_cn: 医院收到了一批书籍捐赠。
words.en: A donation is a gift which is given to a charity or other organization.

words.ex: The evidence is doubtful.
words.ex_cn: 这些证据是可疑的。
words.en: If you are doubtful about something, you are uncertain about it or not sure that it is true or possible.

words.tr: phrase. v. 老是想着；过分关注（某事）； dwelling on 指反复思考或谈论不愉快的事
words.ex: He doesn't dwell on his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他不会纠结于自己的错误。
words.en: If you dwell on something, especially something unpleasant, you think, speak, or write about it a lot or for quite a long time.

words.ex: The new tool enables him to finish work faster.
words.ex_cn: 这个新工具使他能够更快地完成工作。
words.en: If someone or something enables you to do a particular thing, they give you the opportunity or means to do it.

words.tr:
v. 遭遇；遇到；邂逅；
n. 遭遇；
words.ex: He encountered a bear while hiking in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他在森林里徒步时遭遇了一只熊。
words.en: If you encounter problems or difficulties, you experience them.

words.ex: He is impatient when he waits for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时很不耐烦。
words.en: If you are impatient, you are easily annoyed by delays or by people making mistakes.

words.ex: He felt intense pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到剧烈的疼痛。
words.en: If you describe an activity as intense, you mean that it is very serious and concentrated, and often involves doing a great deal in a short time.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.ex: His excuse was laughable.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口可笑极了。
words.en: If you describe something as laughable, you mean that it is so silly or unreasonable that you can only laugh at it.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.ex: Good management helps a company grow.
words.ex_cn: 良好的管理有助于公司发展。
words.en: The control and organization of something, especially a business and its employees.

words.tr: n. 会员资格；全体会员；
words.ex: He paid $50 to get membership of the gym.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了50美元以获得健身房的会员资格。
words.en: Membership is the state of being a member of a group or organization.

words.tr: phrase. 战胜；压倒；胜过；占上风
words.ex: Justice will eventually prevail over evil.
words.ex_cn: 正义终将战胜邪恶。
words.en: To be greater in strength or influence; to triumph.

words.ex: This school uses a progressive teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用一种先进的教学方法。
words.en: A progressive person or idea is one that is modern and new, and is interested in change and improvement.

words.ex: The company plans to recruit new staff next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划下个月招聘新员工。
words.en: To recruit means to enlist someone in the armed forces or to persuade someone to join a company, organization, or group.

words.ex: He shivered in the cold wind.
words.ex_cn: 他在寒风中哆嗦。
words.en: If you shiver, your body shakes slightly because you are cold or frightened.

words.tr:
n. 耸肩
v. 耸肩
words.ex: He shrugged when asked why he was late.
words.ex_cn: 当被问到为什么迟到时，他耸了耸肩。
words.en: If you shrug, you raise your shoulders to show that you are not interested in something or that you do not know or care about something.

words.tr: adj. 精密复杂的；老练的；
words.ex: The phone has a sophisticated camera.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机有一个精密复杂的摄像头。
words.en: A sophisticated person is intelligent and knows a lot, so that they are able to understand complicated situations. A sophisticated machine, device, or method is more advanced or complex than others.

words.ex: He threatened to call the police.
words.ex_cn: 他威胁要叫警察。
words.en: If someone threatens to do something unpleasant to you, or if they threaten you, they say or imply that they will do something unpleasant to you, especially if you do not do what they want.

chapters.name: Unit 6 - Streets full of heroes - Vocabulary

words.ex: They ascribe his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他们把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you ascribe an event or condition to a particular cause, you say or consider that it was caused by that thing.

words.ex: The room was chaotic after the party.
words.ex_cn: 派对后房间一片混乱。
words.en: If a situation, place, or system is chaotic, it is in a state of complete disorder and confusion.

words.ex: The ancient temple has a tall stone column.
words.ex_cn: 这座古庙有一根高大的石柱。
words.en: A column is a tall solid upright stone post used to support a building or as a monument.

words.ex: The correspondent reported the news from the city.
words.ex_cn: 记者从城市报道了新闻。
words.en: A correspondent is someone who reports news from a particular place or on a particular subject for a newspaper, magazine, or television or radio station.

words.tr:
n. 跛子；（身体部分或全部肢体）有缺陷的人
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）
words.ex: The cripple walked slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 那个跛子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is crippled by an injury, it is so serious that they can never move their body properly again. A cripple is a person who is severely disabled or unable to walk because of damage to their body.

words.ex: He wore a decent shirt to the interview.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件像样的衬衫去面试。
words.en: Decent is used to describe something which is considered to be of an acceptable standard or quality.

words.ex: The manager will delegate the task to her assistant.
words.ex_cn: 经理将把这个任务委派给她的助手。
words.en: A delegate is a person who is chosen or elected to vote or make decisions on behalf of a group of people, especially at a conference or a meeting. As a verb, to delegate means to give a task or responsibility to another person, especially someone who is less senior than you.

words.ex: He dominates the conversation.
words.ex_cn: 他主宰了谈话。
words.en: To dominate means to control or govern someone or something, or to be the most important or noticeable feature of something.

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.ex: He is a genius in math.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面是个天才。
words.en: Someone who is a genius is a person who is exceptionally intelligent or talented, especially in a particular field.

words.ex: He showed gratitude for the help.
words.ex_cn: 他表达了对帮助的感激。
words.en: Gratitude is the feeling of being thankful and appreciative.

words.tr:
n. 兽群；
v. 放牧；
words.ex: The herd of cows walked slowly to the pasture.
words.ex_cn: 一群牛缓缓走向牧场。
words.en: A herd is a large group of animals of one kind that live together.

words.tr: n. 英雄表现；英雄气概
words.ex: His heroism saved many lives during the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他的英勇行为在火灾中救了许多人的生命。
words.en: Heroism is great bravery, especially in a difficult situation or in a war.

words.tr: n. 领导才能；领导地位；
words.ex: His leadership helped the team win the match.
words.ex_cn: 他的领导才能帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Leadership is the ability to lead, guide, or direct a group, organization, or country.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.ex: The view from the mountain is marvelous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色极好。
words.en: If you describe something as marvelous, you are emphasizing that it is extremely good.

words.tr: adj. 大规模的；大而重的；
words.ex: The company launched a massive advertising campaign.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司发起了一场大规模的广告活动。
words.en: Something that is massive is extremely large in size, amount, or extent.

words.tr: n. 噩梦；不愉快的经历；
words.ex: He had a nightmare about falling from a tall building.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个从高楼坠落的噩梦。
words.en: A nightmare is a very frightening dream.

words.ex: The manager oversees the team's daily work.
words.ex_cn: 经理监督团队的日常工作。
words.en: To oversee means to watch and direct a piece of work, the people doing it, or the way it is done in order to ensure that it is done correctly.

words.ex: Many families live in the slum near the city center.
words.ex_cn: 许多家庭住在城市中心附近的贫民窟里。
words.en: A slum is a heavily populated urban area characterized by substandard housing and squalor.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.tr: n. 损失；伤亡人数；通行费；
words.ex: The war caused a heavy toll on innocent people.
words.ex_cn: 战争给平民带来了巨大的损失。
words.en: A toll is a small sum of money that you have to pay in order to use a particular bridge or road. / A toll is the total number of deaths, accidents, or disasters that occur in a particular period of time. / When a bell tolls, it rings slowly and repeatedly, often as a sign that someone has died.

words.ex: The play ended in a tragedy when the hero died.
words.ex_cn: 当英雄去世时，这部戏剧以悲剧收场。
words.en: A tragedy is an extremely sad event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 无意识的；无知觉的；
words.ex: He was unconscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他失去了意识。
words.en: If someone is unconscious, they are not awake, usually because they have had a severe injury or illness.

words.ex: He showed the utmost care when handling the fragile glass.
words.ex_cn: 他在处理易碎的玻璃时表现出了最大的小心。
words.en: The greatest or highest degree of something.

chapters.name: Unit 7 - The secret life of science - Vocabulary

words.ex: The two houses are adjacent to each other.
words.ex_cn: 这两栋房子彼此相邻。
words.en: If one thing is adjacent to another, it is next to it or adjoining it.

words.ex: She blends flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To mix substances together so that they combine into a single substance.

words.tr: n. 幸事； v. “bless”的现在分词；
words.ex: Finding a good job after graduation was a blessing.
words.ex_cn: 毕业后找到一份好工作是一件幸事。
words.en: A blessing is a prayer asking for God's favor and protection, or a beneficial thing for which one is grateful.

words.tr:
n. 群；团；簇；
v. 聚集；
words.ex: The stars form a bright cluster in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中形成了一群明亮的星群。
words.en: A cluster of things or people is a small group of them close together.

words.ex: He spoke with confidence during the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲时充满信心。
words.en: Confidence is a feeling of self-assurance arising from one's appreciation of one's own abilities or qualities.

words.ex: The duration of the movie is two hours.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的持续时间是两小时。
words.en: The duration of an event or state is the time during which it happens or exists.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: The police found evidence at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了证据。
words.en: Evidence is anything that you see, experience, read, or are told that causes you to believe that something is true or has really happened.

words.ex: The frequency of the radio station is 101.5 MHz.
words.ex_cn: 这个电台的频率是101.5兆赫。
words.en: The rate at which something happens or is repeated over a particular period of time.

words.tr: adj. 失意的；挫败的； v. “frustrate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt frustrated when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 当他考试不及格时，他感到失意。
words.en: If you are frustrated, you are upset or angry because you are unable to do anything about a situation.

words.tr: adj. 功能的；起作用的；实用的；
words.ex: This chair is functional and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子功能性强且舒适。
words.en: Relating to the way in which something works or operates.

words.ex: He is literally the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他确实是队里最好的球员。
words.en: In a literal manner or sense; exactly.

words.ex: He solved a mathematical problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他很快解决了一个数学问题。
words.en: Relating to or using mathematics; precise and exact.

words.ex: He lost his job, which was a great misfortune.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了工作，这是一场巨大的不幸。
words.en: An unfortunate condition or event.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.tr:
v. 交叠；使部分重叠；
n. 重叠部分；
words.ex: The two colors overlap on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 两种颜色在墙上交叠。
words.en: If one thing overlaps another, or if you overlap them, a part of the first thing occupies the same area as a part of the other thing. You can also say that two things overlap.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.ex: We took a different route to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 我们换了条路线以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: A route is a way from one place to another, or the path that something follows to reach a destination.

words.tr:
n. 袋子；
v. 劫掠；
words.ex: He carried the apples in a burlap sack.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果装在一个麻布袋里。
words.en: A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material, used for storing or carrying goods. It can also refer to the act of dismissing someone from employment or the act of looting a place.

words.ex: He uses a scanner to copy documents.
words.ex_cn: 他使用扫描仪来复制文件。
words.en: A scanner is a device that captures images from photographic prints, posters, magazine pages, and similar sources for computer editing and display.

words.ex: He failed the test, but subsequent efforts helped him pass.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格，但随后的努力让他通过了。
words.en: Following in time or order; succeeding.

words.ex: Subtract 5 from 10 to get 5.
words.ex_cn: 从10中减去5得到5。
words.en: If you subtract one number from another, you take the first number away from the second.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: Children are vulnerable to colds in winter.
words.ex_cn: 儿童在冬天容易感冒。
words.en: If someone or something is vulnerable, they are weak and without protection, with the result that they are easily hurt physically or emotionally.

chapters.name: Unit 8 - High days and holidays - Vocabulary

words.ex: It is advisable to wear a helmet when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是明智的。
words.en: If something is advisable, it will avoid problems if you do it.

words.tr: 短语. 与…和谐一致；与…合为一体
words.ex: She felt at one with nature during her hike in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 她在山中徒步时感到与自然和谐一致。
words.en: In harmony or agreement with someone or something.

words.ex: Her beloved dog always greeted her at the door.
words.ex_cn: 她钟爱的狗总是在门口迎接她。
words.en: Dearly loved.

words.tr: phrase. 偶然遇见；意外碰到
words.ex: I bump into my friend at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我在商店碰到了我的朋友。
words.en: If you bump into someone you know, you meet them unexpectedly.

words.ex: He checks the calendar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看日历。
words.en: A calendar is a chart or device which displays the date and the day of the week, and often the whole of a particular year divided up into months, weeks, and days.

words.ex: Her smile has a special charm.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑有一种特别的魅力。
words.en: If you say that someone has charm, you mean that they behave in a friendly and pleasant way that makes people like them. A charm is also a small ornament that is fixed to a bracelet or necklace.

words.ex: We should conserve water in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 我们应在日常生活中节约用水。
words.en: To conserve something means to protect it from harm, loss, or change, especially in order to preserve it for the future.

words.ex: He dumped the trash into the bin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾倒进了垃圾桶。
words.en: To dump something means to get rid of it quickly and without care, often because it is no longer wanted or needed. It can also refer to the place where waste is left.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.ex: He tried to fill up the hole with sand.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用沙子填补那个洞。
words.en: To make something full, or to become full.

words.ex: He shouted with fury when he lost the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他输掉比赛时，他愤怒地大喊。
words.en: Fury is a feeling of intense anger.

words.ex: Goodness, I didn't expect to see you here!
words.ex_cn: 天哪，我没料到会在这里见到你！
words.en: Goodness is the quality of being kind, helpful, and honest.

words.ex: The gossip about the CEO made everyone shocked.
words.ex_cn: 关于CEO的流言蜚语让所有人都震惊了。
words.en: Gossip is informal conversation or reports about other people's private lives, which might be unkind or not true.

words.tr: adj. 卑微的；谦逊的；虚心的；
words.ex: He lived in a humble house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 他住在河边一座简陋的房子里。
words.en: If you describe someone as humble, you mean that they do not think they are better or more important than other people.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.tr: adj. 东方的（尤指中国和日本）
words.ex: He bought an oriental rug at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一张东方地毯。
words.en: Oriental is used to describe things that come from or are associated with eastern Asia, especially China and Japan.

words.ex: He preaches kindness every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都宣扬仁爱。
words.en: If you preach, you give a talk on a religious or moral subject during a religious service.

words.ex: He gave a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他真诚地道歉了。
words.en: If you say that someone is sincere, you approve of them because they really mean the things they say.

words.ex: He sneaked out of the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上偷偷溜出了房子。
words.en: To move quietly and secretly in order to avoid being noticed.

words.tr: phrase. 留在原地；逗留不走
words.ex: He decided to stick around until the meeting was over.
words.ex_cn: 他决定留下来直到会议结束。
words.en: To remain in a place or situation, especially while waiting for something to happen or someone to arrive.

words.ex: He had to undergo surgery last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周不得不接受手术。
words.en: If you undergo something necessary or unpleasant, it happens to you or is done to you.

words.tr:
n. 真空；空虚；
v. 用真空吸尘器打扫；
words.ex: The vacuum in space keeps no air.
words.ex_cn: 太空中的真空没有空气。
words.en: A vacuum is a space that contains no air or other gas, or a space from which most of the air or gas has been removed. It can also refer to a device that cleans floors and surfaces by sucking up dirt and dust.

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.ex: The youngster rode his bike to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻人每天骑自行车去上学。
words.en: A youngster is a young person, especially a child or teenager.

words.ex: He showed great zeal in helping others.
words.ex_cn: 他在帮助他人时表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Zeal is great enthusiasm, especially in connection with work, religion, or politics.

chapters.name: Unit 9 - What's in a name ? - Vocabulary

words.ex: The administrative office handles school records.
words.ex_cn: 行政办公室负责管理学校档案。
words.en: Relating to the management of a company, organization, or institution.

words.tr: v. 向往；渴望；追求；立志
words.ex: He aspires to be a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他向往成为一名医生。
words.en: If you aspire to something, you have a strong desire to achieve it or attain it.

words.ex: The team comprises five players and one coach.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队包括五名球员和一名教练。
words.en: If you say that something comprises or is comprised of a number of things or people, you mean it has them as its parts or members.

words.ex: The conquest of the mountain took three days.
words.ex_cn: 攻克这座山花了三天时间。
words.en: The act of conquering a place or people.

words.ex: The dominant color in the room is blue.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间占优势的颜色是蓝色。
words.en: Someone or something that is dominant is more powerful, successful, influential, or noticeable than other people or things.

words.ex: The weather is exceedingly cold today.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气极其寒冷。
words.en: To a very great degree; extremely.

words.tr: pron. 他们的；她们的；它们的；
words.ex: Their books are on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他们的书在桌子上。
words.en: You use their to indicate that something belongs or relates to the group of people, animals, or things that you are talking about.

words.tr: adj. 有历史意义的；历史性的；
words.ex: This is a historic moment for our country.
words.ex_cn: 这是对我们国家有历史意义的时刻。
words.en: Something that is historic is important in history, or potentially so.

words.tr: adj. 倾向于…的； v. “incline”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is inclined to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他倾向于帮助别人。
words.en: Having a tendency or preference towards something; likely to do or be something.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.ex: He climbed the ladder to fix the roof.
words.ex_cn: 他爬梯子去修屋顶。
words.en: A ladder is a piece of equipment consisting of a series of steps or rungs fixed between two upright lengths of wood, metal, or rope, used for climbing up or down something.

words.tr: adj. 较低的；下游的；“low”的比较级； v. 降低；
words.ex: He sat in the lower row of the theater.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在剧院的较低一排。
words.en: If you lower something, you move it slowly downwards. If you lower something, you make it less in amount, degree, value, or quality.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.ex: The change in her mood was noticeable.
words.ex_cn: 她情绪的变化显而易见。
words.en: Something that is noticeable is very obvious, so that it is easy to see, hear, or recognize.

words.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
words.ex_cn: 法律迫使司机系安全带。
words.en: If you are obliged to do something, you have to do it because the situation, the law, a duty, etc., makes it necessary.

words.ex: He left home prior to sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 他在日出前离开了家。
words.en: Before a particular time or event.

words.ex: The proportion of students who passed the test was high.
words.ex_cn: 通过考试的学生比例很高。
words.en: A proportion is a part of a whole, or the relationship of one part to another in terms of size, amount, or degree.

words.tr:
adj. 居住的；常驻的；
n. 常住居民；
words.ex: The resident population grew last year.
words.ex_cn: 居住人口去年增加了。
words.en: A resident is someone who lives in a particular place or a person who has their home in a place.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有判断力的；恰当的；合理的；
words.ex: It is sensible to wear a coat in cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 在寒冷的天气里穿外套是明智的。
words.en: A sensible person is able to make good judgments and decisions based on reason rather than emotion.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.ex: He won three successive championships.
words.ex_cn: 他连续赢得了三届冠军。
words.en: Following one after the other without interruption.

words.ex: There was a surge in sales during the holiday season.
words.ex_cn: 假期期间销量激增。
words.en: If something surges, it increases suddenly and greatly, after having been steady or only small in size or amount.

words.tr: v. 销声匿迹；突然消失；
words.ex: The magic trick made the coin vanish.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让硬币销声匿迹了。
words.en: If someone or something vanishes, they disappear suddenly or in a way that cannot be explained.

chapters.name: Unit 10 - Tales ancient and modern - Vocabulary

words.ex: The country is on the brink of war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正处于战争的边缘。
words.en: If you are on the brink of something, you are about to do it or experience it.

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

words.ex: The hiker stood at the edge of the cliff.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者站在悬崖边上。
words.en: A cliff is a high area of rock with a very steep side, often at the edge of the sea or a river.

words.ex: His converse was the opposite of what he said earlier.
words.ex_cn: 他的相反言论与他之前说的话相反。
words.en: To engage in conversation; to talk informally with someone.

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful creation of the artist.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是艺术家的一个美丽作品。
words.en: The act or process of bringing something into existence.

words.ex: He deliberately broke the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他有意地违反了规则。
words.en: If you do something deliberately, you do it intentionally or after thinking about it carefully.

words.ex: He will depart tomorrow morning.
words.ex_cn: 他明天早上离开。
words.en: If you depart from a place, you leave it and start a journey to another place.

words.tr: phrase. 处理好；处置掉；除掉
words.ex: Please dispose of the trash before you leave.
words.ex_cn: 请在离开前处理好垃圾。
words.en: To get rid of something that you no longer want or need.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

words.tr:
n. 仙子；小精灵；
adj. 幻想中的；
words.ex: The little girl saw a fairy in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 小女孩在花园里看到了一位仙子。
words.en: A fairy is a mythical being of folklore and romance usually having magic powers and dwelling on earth in close relationship with humans.

words.ex: He heard a footstep behind him.
words.ex_cn: 他听到身后有脚步声。
words.en: A footstep is the sound or mark that is made by someone walking each time their foot touches the ground.

words.tr: adj. 不感兴趣的；不关心的；
words.ex: He was indifferent to the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影不感兴趣。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being indifferent to something, you mean that they have a complete lack of interest in it.

words.tr: adj. 误导的； v. “mislead”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ad is misleading because it shows fake results.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告是误导的，因为它展示了虚假的结果。
words.en: If you describe something as misleading, you mean that it gives you a wrong idea or impression.

words.ex: He always follows his morality in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他日常生活中总是遵循自己的道德。
words.en: Morality is the belief that some behaviour is right and acceptable and that other behaviour is wrong.

words.ex: It's a myth that eating late at night causes weight gain.
words.ex_cn: 晚上吃东西会导致发胖，这是一种错误观念。
words.en: A myth is a traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon, and typically involving supernatural beings or events.

words.tr:
v. 投入；跳入
n. 跳进；骤降
words.ex: He plunged into the cold water.
words.ex_cn: 他跳进了冰冷的水里。
words.en: If something or someone plunges in a particular direction, especially into water, they fall, rush, or throw themselves in that direction.

words.ex: He will renew his passport next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会更新他的护照。
words.en: To renew something means to begin it again or to make it new again.

words.tr:
n. 谣言
v. 谣传
words.ex: There is a rumour that he will quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 有一个传言说他要辞职。
words.en: A rumour is a story or piece of information that may or may not be true, but that people are talking about.

words.tr: adj. 中等的；次要的；第二的；
words.ex: He attends a secondary school in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城里上一所中学。
words.en: If you describe something as secondary, you mean that it is less important than something else.

words.tr:
v. 弯腰；俯身；卑屈；俯冲
n. 弯腰；屈背；屈服；俯冲
words.ex: He must stoop to enter the small door.
words.ex_cn: 他必须弯腰才能进入那扇小门。
words.en: If someone stoops, they bend their body forwards and downwards.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.
